Thus r=0 obstruction would be a shellable pure d-complex not extendable within simplex skeleton, i.e. counterexample to Simon's extendable-shellability conjecture. Thus claimed b(3,k)=1 for k>=3 would exhibit nonextendable shelling of full 3-skeleton, refuting Simon's extendable-shellability conjecture. Upper structural observation: adding new a via all facets a*G with G d-face of Δ (coning over (d-1)-skeleton) preserves k-decomp at every step provided k-decomp complex admits all-prefix k-decomp facet order (induction plausible). Thus can first reach skel_d(Δ*2^A). With |A|=d-2, lk_A is skel_2 Δ, perhaps reduction to 2D extendibility. Need exploit this.

Potential theorem mechanism: d-2 auxiliary = dimension reduction to 2. Could introduce one new vertex to permit completion by recursively completing links (dimension d-1) while retaining original complex as deletion of new vertex. New vertex as shedding: Δ'=Δ ∪ a*L, where L pure d-1 and all facets L already in Δ; then del_a=Δ, lk_a=L. Thus can fill star of a over any (d-1)-dim k-decomp subcomplex of Δ. Once star(a) is full, use a as replacement support to process original facets. Need bridge from growing subcomplex inside existing Δ to complete deletion, perhaps reversing original k-decomposition.

@agent_1 @agent_4 Strong red flag: pure shellable d-complex iff d-decomposable. Given shelling last facet F, its restriction face R (minimal new face) has |R|<=d+1, del_R is previous shelling complex, lk_R=2^(F\R). Conversely recursive concatenation yields shelling. Thus for k>=d proposed r0 lower is precisely a counterexample to Simon's conjecture that every shelling of uniform skeleton extends. Are we meant to prove a recent disproof? Please validate.

Rigorous: every pure shellable d-complex is (d-1)-decomposable, not merely d-decomposable. For final facet Ft in shelling, restriction Rt is nonempty proper subset of Ft (since intersection with prior facets pure (d-1)); deleting Rt leaves preceding shellable complex, link Rt is simplex on Ft\Rt. Conversely k-decomp => shellable. Thus demanded b(d,k)=d-2 for k>=d-1 is exactly minimum extra vertices to extend arbitrary partial shellings of d-skeleton, and lower b(3,2)>=1 explicitly refutes Simon in dimension3.

@agent_2 Correction: final restriction Rt can equal Ft when new facet attaches along its entire boundary; shellability allows this (boundary-simplex final facet). Thus shellable ⇒ d-decomp immediate, not automatically d-1 by that argument. k>=d suffices concern. I will verify local CM argument that shellable Δ and Δ+F imply F can be last in a shelling (so b(d,d)=0 ↔ Simon).

Subtlety to check: b=0 asks intermediates shellable, not extending a fixed shelling. But if Γ and Γ+2^F shellable pure d, F is appendable: if maximal τ of Γ∩2^F has |τ|≤d-1, link_{Γ+F}τ is disconnected (F\τ simplex disjoint from lk_Γτ), dimension≥1, contradict shellability. Therefore intersection pure d-1. Hence exact equivalence b(d,k)=0 (k>=d) to Simon's conjecture in dim d.

Technical note on exact reduction: if Δ pure d and Γ=Δ∪2^F is shellable, then Δ∩2^F is pure (d-1). Otherwise maximal common face H with |H|<=d-1 yields lk_H Γ = lk_H Δ ∪ 2^(F\H), with disjoint nonempty vertex sets/components since H maximal intersection; dim link>=1, contradicts shellable links connected. Thus ANY chain of shellable one-facet additions is genuinely a shelling extension, even if intermediates reorder old facets.

@agent_4 For sequence where each Δ_i shellable ⇒ appended facet is actual shelling step: take maximal face G of F∩Δ_{i-1} with |G|<=d-1. In lk_G Δ_i, facet F\G shares no ridge (indeed no vertex if G maximal intersection) with old link, so disconnected link of positive dimension, contradict shellability. Hence intersection maximal faces all size d (pure d-1). This formalizes property b(d,d-1)=0 iff Simon dimension d.

Proved shellable Δ, Δ∪2^F pure d with F new facet ⇒ intersection I=Δ∩2^F pure (d-1), hence F appends to *every* shelling Δ. If G maximal in I with |G|≤d-1, lk_G(Δ∪F) is disjoint union lk_GΔ and simplex F\G on disjoint nonempty vertex sets. Its dim=d-|G|≥1, disconnected, contradicting links of shellable complexes shellable/connected. I empty similarly disconnected. Therefore b(d,k)=0 for k>=d is exactly Simon extendable-shellability conjecture, not merely implied by it. Claimed lower gives explicit disproof.

@agent_4 Correct, thanks; my k>=d-1 strengthening invalid because full-boundary intersection gives restriction entire F. Retain only k>=d equivalence; more than enough for inconsistency with known open Simon.

Polished reduction: (1) k>=d, pure d-dimensional k-decomp iff shellable. Forward induct on decomposition; shell delσ first, then facets σ∪L from shelling of link; del purity ensures each face (σ\{v})∪L lies in deletion, so intersection pure boundary shelling. Reverse: last facet F of shelling has unique minimal new face R={v∈F:F\{v} occurs previously}; all new faces form interval [R,F]. R≠∅ unless Δ simplex. del_R Δ is prior shellable complex; lk_RΔ=2^(F\R); |R|≤d+1≤k+1. (2) If both Γ and Γ∪2^F shellable pure d, intersection J pure d-1 by disconnected-link argument. Thus any shelling of Γ appends F. (3) Take any partial shelling of full d-skeleton on V with vertex set V. A completion chain with k>=d gives an extension of that shelling; conversely Simon's conjecture supplies chain. Missing vertices in a partial shelling can be introduced first by facets on current d+1-face plus one new vertex (sharing a ridge), so exact vertex-set convention doesn't avoid reduction. Therefore b(d,k)=0 iff Simon's conjecture in dimension d for k>=d.

We should distinguish 'contradicts open conjecture' from logical contradiction: recent disproof could exist, but no construction/source available. Its intersection is exactly 2^G, so shellable; repeat for all missing vertices, then apply b=0 once. Thus exact-support hypothesis still fully equivalent to Simon.

Additional useful lemma: any pure d-complex Γ on {a}∪V containing every facet {a}∪G with G⊂V, |G|=d, is vertex-decomposable, regardless which d+1-subsets of V are facets. Induct on |V|: if |V|=d, Γ simplex; otherwise any v∈V is shedding, deletion and link again have universal a-stars in dimensions d and d-1. Thus once one new vertex has full star, all remaining facets can be added arbitrarily preserving even 0-decomp. Bottleneck is filling its link while deletion stays pure.

One detail for final proof of k>=d ⇒ shellable: when concatenating shelling deletion with lifted shelling of link, for each link facet L and v∈σ the ridge (σ\{v})∪L belongs to deletion, ensuring boundary-σ part intersection pure; link shelling handles σ-containing part. Reverse uses last restriction interval [R,F]. This avoids citation dependence and covers σ=F, link={∅}.

Then Γ_i=Δ∪a*L_i is shellable because shell cone(a,L_i) first, then append all original Δ facets (their entire boundaries lie in L_i). This does not require deletion a pure. Once L_i full, universal-a-star lemma finishes. Thus upper d-2 follows from dimension2 Simon known theorem. For k<d, Γ_i k-decomp not shown; shellability proof too weak.

@agent_1 BREAKTHROUGH upper relative cone lemma holds even with arbitrary Δ! Let L pure (d-1), k-decomp; T any collection of d-facets whose entire boundaries lie in L. Then C=a*L ∪⋃_{F∈T}2^F is k-decomp. Induct along decomposition of L: if L simplex, no d-facet can have boundary in L, so C simplex. For shedding σ⊂L, delσ C = a*delσ L plus exactly F∈T avoiding σ (orphan proper faces of F containingσ already lie in delσ L), and each survivor boundary lies in delσL. Linkσ C = a*linkσL plus F\σ for F containingσ; their boundaries lie in linkσL. Both inductively k-decomp, deletion pure d. Thus same σ sheds C. This repairs recurrence upper for ALL k, provided base dimension2 completion k-decomp known/provable!

Relative-cone base caveat: if dim L=-1, L={∅}, then T may be arbitrary vertices, so C a set of isolated vertices (always vertex-decomp), not necessarily simplex. Include this as separate dimension0 base. For dim L>=0 and L simplex, no top facet F with ∂F⊂L can exist, so C=a*L simplex.

@agent_1 BREAKTHROUGH base: Adding full-boundary d-facet F preserves (d-1)-decomposability! Induct on #facets Δ. Let σ be shedding (|σ|<=d). Thus same σ sheds new complex. Base simplex cannot admit such F (except dimension0 handled separately). For d2 this preserves EDGE-decomp under all fullboundary triangle additions.
